success: In the suitable branch: shed hair reduced, pet stress stayed below threshold, brushing stopped at the first stress spike, hair collected; in the unsuitable branch: no brushing and an owner report.
wrong: Keeps brushing while the cat swats/growls.
Brushes over a hot spot or pulls at a mat.
Uses a wire slicker hard on a short-haired dog's skin.
fidelity: P: brush contact force on coat/skin
notes: Keyword 'where appropriate' -> suitability branch.

interpretation: When a dog comes in muddy, keep it at the entry (leash/wait) and wipe all four paws, including between the pads, with a damp towel or paw wipe, then dry them before it walks on clean floors.
success: All four paws' mud level below threshold before the dog crosses onto clean flooring; zero mud tracks indoors; pet stress below threshold.
wrong: Wipes only the front paws.
Lets the dog in first and wipes afterward (tracks everywhere).
Uses household cleaning wipes that are toxic if licked.
notes: Entry/return-from-walk routine link.

interpretation: Clean the pet's bed: shake it outside, remove hair with a vacuum or lint roller, then wash the cover per its label with unscented detergent and dry fully, or spot-clean a non-removable bed and its foam insert.
conditional: Bed construction: removable cover -> remove, machine wash, dry; non-removable -> vacuum, spot clean, air dry. Randomized.
success: Bed hair/odor below threshold, fully dry before returning, foam insert not machine washed; pet has its bed back.
wrong: Washes the foam insert in the washer (destroyed).
Puts it back damp.
Throws the hairy bed straight into the washer (drain clog).
notes: Pairs with 'Wash pet blankets'.

interpretation: Wash pet blankets: shake/lint-roll off hair first, wash separately from the family's laundry with unscented detergent on hot with an extra rinse, dry, and clear the lint trap and washer drum of hair afterward.
success: Blankets clean and dry; no pet hair transferred to human laundry; lint trap cleared and drum free of hair after the cycle.
wrong: Washes blankets with the family's clothes.
Skips removing hair first.
Leaves the lint trap packed with hair (fire risk).
notes: Laundry-load separation rule is a household preference.

interpretation: Swap soiled pet bedding for fresh, species-appropriate bedding: for small animals, replace soiled substrate with safe paper/aspen bedding at proper depth while keeping a little clean familiar nest material; for dogs/cats, swap in a clean blanket or cover.
success: Soiled bedding removed to sealed trash; fresh safe bedding at target depth; part of the clean nest retained; no cedar/pine bedding for small animals; animal returned and stress low.
wrong: Uses cedar shavings for a hamster.
Throws out the entire nest including the hidden food stash.
Leaves the soiled bedding bag open indoors.
notes: Covers small-animal cage and dog/cat bed variants.

interpretation: Scoop the litter box: remove all clumps and feces, leave clean litter, bag and tie the waste for the outdoor trash (never flush), note abnormal output (blood, diarrhea, no urine clumps) for the owner, and wash hands/clean the scoop.
success: Clump/feces count in the box = 0, litter depth still above minimum, waste bagged and in the outdoor bin, none flushed; abnormal output reported when present.
wrong: Flushes clumps down the toilet.
Leaves clumps buried at the bottom.
Ignores blood in the urine clumps.
notes: Litter family (refill, change, clean, sweep).

interpretation: Top up the litter box to the recommended depth (about 5-7 cm) with the same litter type the cat already uses, pouring low to avoid dust clouds and spills.
success: Litter depth within the target band; litter type identical to existing; spill outside the box below threshold; cat continues using the box.
wrong: Overfills so the cat kicks litter out.
Tops up with a different scented litter (box avoidance).
Pours from height spilling onto the floor.
fidelity: P: granular pour volume and spill
notes: Granular-material pouring skill.

interpretation: Fully change the litter: empty all used litter into a bag, wash the box with mild unscented soap (no ammonia, no bleach residue, no essential oils), dry it completely, refill with fresh litter to depth, and return it to the same spot.
success: All old litter removed and bagged outside; box clean, dry and free of ammonia/bleach/oil residue; fresh litter at depth; box back at its original location.
wrong: Cleans with ammonia or mixes bleach with ammonia (toxic, deters cat).
Refills while the box is still wet.
Moves the box to a new location.
notes: Overlaps 'Clean litter box'; this one emphasizes full litter replacement.

interpretation: Clean up litter tracked around the box: shake the litter mat into the trash, sweep or vacuum scattered granules within about a meter, and do it while the cat is not using the box.
success: Granule count within the zone below threshold, mat clean, nothing swept toward food bowls; cat not startled while in the box.
wrong: Wet-mops clumping litter into paste.
Vacuums loudly while the cat is in the box.
Sweeps litter under the fridge or toward the food bowls.
notes: Sweep skill shared with floor cleaning.

interpretation: Deep-clean the litter box itself: after emptying, scrub urine scale and odor with warm water and a pet-safe cleaner (or enzymatic cleaner), give the required dwell time, rinse thoroughly, dry, and refill.
success: Box odor/scale soil below threshold, cleaner fully rinsed, dry, refilled and returned; tub/sink used is disinfected afterward if used.
wrong: Wipes without dwell time (odor remains).
Leaves cleaner residue/fragrance (box avoidance).
Scrubs it in the kitchen sink.
notes: Overlaps 'Change litter'; this one is about the box surface.

interpretation: Find and pick up all dog waste in the yard (including in tall grass and along fence lines) with a bag or scooper without smearing, tie the bags, put them in the outdoor trash, and avoid stepping in any and tracking it indoors.
success: Yard dog-waste count = 0, all in tied bags in the outdoor trash (not recycling/compost/yard-waste); no waste on robot feet entering the house; scooper rinsed.
wrong: Misses piles along the fence line and in tall grass.
Steps in waste and tracks it inside.
Puts bags in the compost or recycling bin.
notes: Search-coverage task outdoors.

interpretation: Dispose of collected pet waste (dog poop bags, cat litter clumps, soiled small-animal bedding) into the correct waste stream per local rules: sealed in a bag in the outdoor trash, never in recycling, compost or the toilet for cat litter.
conditional: Waste type/local rule: cat litter and bagged dog waste -> outdoor trash; small-animal herbivore bedding (paper/aspen) -> compost only where the household permits it; never flush cat litter. Randomized household/municipal rule.
success: Every pet-waste item ends in the stream allowed by the scenario's rules; nothing in recycling; no cat litter flushed; indoor bins not left holding pet waste overnight.
wrong: Flushes cat litter.
Puts poop bags in recycling.
Leaves an open bag of waste in the kitchen bin.
notes: Waste-stream rules shared with cleaning trash/recycling entries.

interpretation: Let the dog (or other outdoor-allowed pet) out into the yard after checking the yard is secure and the weather is acceptable, without letting indoor-only pets slip out, and keep track of how long it is out.
conditional: Yard/pet check: gate closed, fence intact, weather OK, pet allowed outdoors -> open the door for that pet only; gate open/fence breach/storm/extreme heat or cold, or pet is indoor-only -> do not let it out (close the gate first if allowed, otherwise report). Randomized.
success: Intended pet is in a secured yard; indoor-only cat still inside; gate latched; no escape events; time-outside tracked for recall.
wrong: Opens the door while the side gate is open (dog escapes).
Lets the indoor-only cat dart out.
Puts the dog out during a thunderstorm or heat wave.
notes: Pairs with 'Let pet back inside'.

interpretation: Bring the pets back inside: call them in, ensure every pet that went out has come back (count), wipe muddy paws at the door, keep wildlife or neighbor animals out, and close/lock the door.
success: All pets that went out are inside; door closed and locked per routine; no outside animal inside; no mud tracked.
wrong: Closes the door before the second dog comes back.
Lets the neighbor's cat in.
Lets a muddy dog run onto the carpet.
notes: Counts are the core predicate.

interpretation: Set the pet door to allow passage (open both ways, or in-only/out-only as instructed) by removing the locking panel or changing the dial/microchip setting, respecting the household's night-lock rule.
conditional: Household rule/time: daytime or rule allows -> unlock to the requested mode; night when the rule says locked (wildlife) -> do not open unless an adult explicitly overrides. Randomized time.
success: Pet door mode equals the requested mode and the intended pet can pass (simulated pass test); rule-violating requests at night refused/escalated; flap intact.
wrong: Removes the flap entirely.
Sets in-only when out was intended so the pet is stuck.
Opens it at night against the rule (raccoon enters).
notes: Pairs with 'Secure pet door'.

interpretation: Lock the pet door after confirming every pet is on the intended side (usually inside), inserting the locking panel or setting the lock mode, and verify with a push test.
success: Pet door blocks passage both ways (push test fails to pass); all pets on the intended side; no pet caught in the flap.
wrong: Locks it while the dog is still outside.
Slides the panel in without latching it.
Locks while the cat is halfway through.
notes: Night/away routine component.

interpretation: Attach the leash to the load-bearing D-ring of a properly fitted collar or harness (two-finger fit, buckles closed), indoors with the door still closed, while the dog is calm.
success: Leash clip latched on the load-bearing ring (not the tag ring); collar/harness fit within tolerance and buckled; door opened only after attachment.
wrong: Clips to the ID-tag split ring.
Attaches to a loose collar the dog backs out of.
Opens the front door before clipping on.
notes: Leash primitives (attach/remove/hang).

interpretation: Unclip the leash only once the dog is inside with the door closed (or in a secured, gated yard), never on the street or with the door open.
success: Leash detached only when the door/gate is closed; dog remains in the secured space; leash then put away.
wrong: Unclips on the doorstep with the door open.
Unclips in an unfenced front yard.
Removes the harness and leash together and drops them.
notes: Followed by 'Hang leash'.

interpretation: Hang the leash (and harness) on its designated hook by the door, untangled and not dragging on the floor or within reach of a dog that chews.
success: Leash hangs from the designated hook (stable loop), untangled, end above floor and out of dog reach; not on the doorknob.
wrong: Drops it on the floor by the door (trip/chew).
Hangs it on the doorknob so it falls when the door opens.
Stuffs it tangled into a drawer.
notes: Simple hook-hanging primitive in pet context.

interpretation: Assemble a walk kit at the door matched to the pet, time and weather: leash and harness, at least two waste bags, treats, water and a collapsible bowl in heat, reflective gear/light at night, coat or booties in cold/salted conditions.
conditional: Conditions: night -> add reflective vest/light; hot -> water + bowl; cold/snow/salt -> coat/booties; mild daytime -> those extras not required. Randomized weather/time.
success: Kit at the door contains all scenario-required items and the correct pet's gear; waste bag count >= 2; low stock reported.
wrong: Forgets waste bags.
Brings the cat harness for the dog.
Ignores the weather (no water in a heat wave, no light at night).
notes: Checklist pattern.

interpretation: Walk the dog on leash along a neighborhood route: control pulling, stop at curbs, avoid traffic and other dogs, prevent eating litter/bones, check pavement heat, pick up waste, and return home within the planned time without ever dropping the leash.
success: Dog home safely within budget; leash attached the whole time; zero road incursions; zero forbidden-item ingestion; every waste event picked up; no walks on pavement above the heat threshold.
wrong: Drops the leash when the dog lunges.
Lets the dog eat a chicken bone.
Leaves waste on a neighbor's lawn or walks on scorching asphalt.
fidelity: G: leash length constraint and sidewalk/traffic geometry
notes: Off-property errand; needs owner approval of route.

interpretation: Keep track of where each pet is over time (rooms, yard, hiding spots), notice escapes or entry into restricted areas (open gate, nursery, kitchen while cooking), and report promptly without chasing the pet.
success: Location log matches ground truth within the allowed error count; escapes/restricted-zone entries reported within T seconds; no false 'escaped' alarm for a cat hiding in a closet; pet not chased.
wrong: Reports a stale last-seen location without updating.
Declares the cat escaped while it hides in a closet.
Chases the pet around the house.
notes: Monitoring/standing task.

interpretation: Check every pet's water source (bowls, fountain, cage bottle, outdoor bowl in heat) for adequate clean water and fix only what needs fixing.
conditional: Level/condition: below threshold, dirty, or fountain pump stopped -> refill/clean/restart (or report if not possible); adequate and clean -> leave untouched. Randomized states.
success: After the check, every pet has a clean water source above threshold; sources that were fine were not disturbed; report lists what was refilled.
wrong: Refills nothing because 'there is some water'.
Misses the rabbit's cage bottle with a stuck nozzle.
Empties and refills every bowl regardless (unneeded churn) while missing the outdoor bowl.
notes: Check-then-fix pattern.

interpretation: Refill a caged bird's food dish: first close windows/doors and stop ceiling fans, open the cage carefully, blow off or discard empty seed hulls (a dish of hulls can look full), add the correct seed/pellets, and relatch the cage.
success: Dish contains edible food (hull fraction below threshold) at the target amount; bird stayed in the cage; door latched; fan was off and windows closed while the cage was open.
wrong: Tops up a dish of hulls so most of it is still empty husks.
Leaves the cage door unlatched.
Opens the cage with a fan running and window open (escape/injury).
notes: Hull-vs-seed perception trap.

interpretation: Replace the bird's water with fresh water daily: remove droppings/seed-contaminated water, clean the dish or bottle, refill, verify the bottle nozzle flows, and relatch the cage.
success: Fresh clean water present (no droppings), nozzle flows if a bottle; bird remained caged; door latched.
wrong: Tops up dirty water.
Refills a bottle with a stuck ball valve.
Leaves the cage open.
notes: Bird care family.

interpretation: Wash the bird's food and water dishes with hot water and mild soap or a bird-safe cleaner, avoiding aerosols or strong fumes near the bird, rinse, dry fully, and swap in spare clean dishes so the bird is never without food and water.
success: Dishes soil-free, dry, returned; spare dishes in place during cleaning; no aerosol/fume exposure near the bird.
wrong: Sprays an aerosol cleaner next to the cage.
Returns a wet seed dish (mold).
Leaves the bird without water for hours.
notes: Bird-safe chemical rule.

interpretation: Slide out the cage tray, fold up and remove the soiled liner without scattering droppings and seed husks, insert a fresh plain paper liner cut to fit, and reseat the tray fully so there is no gap the bird can escape through.
success: Fresh liner fits the tray, tray fully seated (gap ~0), soiled liner in the trash, debris on floor below threshold, bird still caged.
wrong: Uses a scented or cedar liner.
Leaves the tray half-out leaving a gap.
Shakes droppings onto the floor.
notes: Bird/small-animal cage maintenance.

interpretation: Wipe the outside of the cage (bars, base, surrounding floor/wall) with a bird-safe cleaner on a cloth (never sprayed toward the bird or into food), rinse residue the bird could touch, and keep the cage door latched.
success: Exterior soil below threshold; no cleaner on the bird, food or water; no residue on bars; door latched; bird stress low.
wrong: Sprays cleaner into the cage onto the bird/food.
Uses bleach and leaves it unrinsed.
Opens the door to reach and leaves it open.
notes: Pairs with 'Clean aquarium exterior' (pet-safe exterior cleaning).

interpretation: Clean the outside glass/acrylic of the aquarium and the hood with an aquarium-safe cleaner or plain damp microfiber, never spraying ammonia glass cleaner near the open top, without bumping the tank or disturbing heater/filter cords.
success: Exterior streak/fingerprint soil below threshold; tank water ammonia/contaminant unchanged; acrylic unscratched; heater and filter still powered; lid back on.
wrong: Sprays ammonia glass cleaner near the open top (contaminates water).
Uses an abrasive pad on an acrylic tank.
Unplugs the filter/heater to clean and forgets to replug.
notes: Pet-safe chemical rule.

interpretation: Feed the aquarium fish the species-appropriate food in a small amount they finish within about two minutes, once per scheduled feeding (check the log so other residents' feedings are not doubled), and remove uneaten food.
success: Food amount within +/-20% of the prescribed ration; uneaten food after 5 min ~0 (or removed); bottom-dwellers get sinking food; log updated; no double feeding.
wrong: Dumps a large pinch so food rots on the bottom.
Feeds again after someone already did.
Gives only floating flakes to bottom feeders.
notes: Feeding-log anti-double-feed predicate shared with dog/cat feeding.

interpretation: Turn the aquarium light on or off as wanted/scheduled (roughly 8-10 h photoperiod), using the light's own switch or timer, without unplugging the heater or filter on the same power strip.
success: Light state equals the desired state; heater and filter remain powered; photoperiod over the day stays within the band.
wrong: Unplugs the filter or heater instead of the light.
Leaves the light on 24 h (algae).
Turns it off while the owner is viewing the tank.
user_sim: Hidden: desired state when phrasing is the bare 'the tank light'. Necessary question only if schedule and request conflict.
notes: On/off entry; same power-strip disambiguation as 'Turn lights off in unused rooms'.

interpretation: Notice unusual pet behavior or symptoms (lethargy, not eating, vomiting, limping, labored breathing, excessive thirst, signs of toxin ingestion like a chewed chocolate wrapper) and report them to the owner with what, when and where, escalating urgent signs, without giving any medication or home remedy.
conditional: Severity: urgent signs (suspected toxin, breathing difficulty, seizure, collapse) -> immediate alert to owner with emergency-vet suggestion, preserve evidence; mild/unclear -> normal-priority report; normal behavior (sleeping dog) -> no report. Randomized.
success: Report names the correct pet, symptoms, onset time and severity; urgent cases alerted within seconds; evidence preserved; zero medication/remedy actions; no false reports on normal behavior.
wrong: Gives the dog human pain medication or induces vomiting.
Ignores or delays an urgent sign.
Floods the owner with alarms about normal napping.
notes: Explicit 'rather than guessing at medical treatment' -> report-only policy.

interpretation: Identify each houseplant's species (e.g. pothos, snake plant, peace lily, fiddle-leaf fig, jade, lily) to derive its care profile, flag species toxic to the household's pets, recognize artificial plants, and say 'unsure' instead of guessing.
success: Plant registry labels match ground truth for identified plants (accuracy above threshold) with low-confidence ones marked unsure; all pet-toxic plants flagged when pets live there; artificial plants marked artificial.
wrong: Confidently mislabels a peace lily as a calla.
Misses that a true lily is in a home with a cat.
Registers an artificial plant as living (later waters it).
notes: Feeds care-profile lookups for all plant entries.

interpretation: Check each potted plant's soil moisture at root depth (finger 2-5 cm or a moisture meter), classify dry/moist/wet relative to that species' needs, and report which plants need water without watering them.
success: Per-plant classification and needs-water decision match ground truth (surface-dry but deep-wet pots classified as wet); no plant watered; no root damage from probing.
wrong: Judges by the surface only.
Waters while 'checking'.
Uses one moisture rule for both succulent and fern.
notes: Check-only; feeds 'Water houseplants'.

interpretation: Water indoor plants according to each species' needs and current soil moisture: water only those that are dry enough, thoroughly until drainage for pots with holes, sparingly for pots without, little for succulents, at the soil not on fuzzy leaves.
conditional: Soil moisture vs species: dry for its species -> water the right amount; still moist -> skip (overwatering causes rot). Randomized moisture so a fixed schedule fails.
success: Every living plant ends within its moisture band; moist plants not watered; saucers don't overflow onto furniture/floors; no water on leaves of sensitive species; artificial plants dry.
wrong: Waters every plant the same amount on schedule.
Overflows a saucer onto a wood table.
Waters the artificial plant.
fidelity: P: water volume vs soil absorption and saucer overflow
notes: Core watering skill shared with outdoor potted plants and garden beds.

interpretation: Water potted plants on the patio/porch with a can or hose, accounting for recent and forecast rain and heat (terracotta and small pots dry faster), watering deeply at the soil, ideally in the morning, then shutting off and coiling the hose.
conditional: Weather: rained recently or rain imminent -> skip (or water only pots under cover that stayed dry); hot and dry -> water thoroughly. Randomized weather.
success: Each pot ends within its moisture band given weather; no watering right after heavy rain except sheltered pots; spigot off and hose coiled.
wrong: Waters right after a downpour.
Skips the sheltered pots that stayed dry under the roof.
Leaves the spigot running or dripping.
fidelity: P: water volume vs soil absorption
notes: Weather-aware variant of watering.

interpretation: Deep-water garden beds at the root zone (soaker hose, drip, or wand at soil level) to the needed depth, avoiding wetting disease-prone foliage and runoff onto paths, and obeying local watering-day restrictions.
conditional: Rain/restriction: recent rainfall covered the weekly need or today is a restricted day -> skip; dry and allowed -> water to depth. Randomized.
success: Root-zone moisture within band across the bed; no runoff onto paths; foliage of disease-prone plants dry; restrictions obeyed; spigot off.
wrong: Sprays overhead at dusk soaking tomato leaves.
Waters on a restricted day.
Lets water run off onto the walkway.
notes: Garden-bed watering; overlaps outdoor sections' irrigation entries.

interpretation: About 30 minutes after watering, empty standing water from plant saucers without spilling, using a baster/sponge for heavy pots instead of lifting them, while leaving intentional pebble humidity trays alone.
conditional: Saucer type: plain saucer with standing water -> empty it; pebble humidity tray where water stays below the pebble tops -> leave it. Randomized.
success: No plain saucer holds standing water; pebble trays keep water below pebble tops; floor spill below threshold; heavy pots not tipped.
wrong: Tilts a full saucer under a heavy pot and spills.
Empties the pebble humidity tray.
Leaves the water standing.
fidelity: P: liquid volume, tilt and spill
notes: Container-emptying skill shared with dehumidifier bucket.

interpretation: Turn potted plants a quarter to half turn so they grow evenly toward the light, except budding/flowering plants that drop buds when moved; lift rather than drag heavy pots.
conditional: Plant state: leaning non-sensitive plant -> rotate 90-180 deg; plant in bud/flower that drops buds when moved (Christmas cactus, gardenia) -> do not rotate. Randomized.
success: Rotated plants' yaw changed by 90-180 deg and lean decreases over simulated days; budding sensitive plants untouched (zero bud drops); no floor scratches.
wrong: Rotates a full 360 deg (no change).
Rotates the budding Christmas cactus.
Drags heavy pots across the floor.
notes: Orientation primitive in plant context.

interpretation: Move plants that show low-light symptoms (leggy, pale, leaning) to brighter spots suited to their species, without putting low-light plants in scorching direct sun, blocking windows/egress, or putting pet-toxic plants within pet reach.
success: Each moved plant's modeled daily light within its species band; no scorch; window operation and walkways unblocked; toxic plants out of pet reach; no plant on a radiator.
wrong: Moves a fern into a scorching south window.
Places a pot on the radiator sill.
Blocks the window or a walkway with a big plant.
notes: Pairs with 'Move plants away from excess heat'.

interpretation: Relocate plants that sit too close to heat sources (radiators, heat vents, space heaters, oven, hot afternoon window glass) to spots that are cooler but still bright enough and not in cold drafts.
success: No plant remains in a zone above its species' max temperature; new spots meet the light band and are outside AC/cold-draft zones.
wrong: Moves it into a dark closet.
Puts it right under the AC vent.
Moves only one of the affected plants.
notes: Thermal zone model shared with climate.

interpretation: Remove dust from houseplant leaves with a soft dry brush or dry microfiber, supporting each leaf from beneath, using only a soft brush on fuzzy leaves, and no leaf-shine oils.
success: Leaf dust below threshold on all reachable leaves; zero torn/snapped leaves; no oil/shine product applied; fuzzy leaves only brushed.
wrong: Uses leaf-shine oil.
Pulls leaves without support, tearing them.
Wipes fuzzy African violet leaves with a wet cloth.
notes: Pairs with 'Wipe plant leaves'; same plant-dust soil.

interpretation: Wipe smooth plant leaves with a cloth dampened in lukewarm water, supporting each leaf, to remove dust and residue, but not wet-wipe fuzzy leaves or succulents with a powdery bloom.
conditional: Leaf type: smooth glossy leaves (fig, rubber plant, monstera) -> damp wipe; fuzzy leaves (African violet) or farina-coated succulents (echeveria) -> do NOT wet-wipe (soft dry brush or leave). Randomized species mix.
success: Smooth leaves dust-free and not dripping; fuzzy and farina-coated plants unwiped (farina intact); no torn leaves.
wrong: Wet-wipes the echeveria, removing its protective bloom.
Wipes African violet leaves (spotting/rot).
Uses cold soapy water dripping into the soil.
notes: Leaf-type branch randomized.

interpretation: Remove leaves that are fully dead (brown and dry) at their base with clean snips or a gentle tug only if they release easily, leaving yellowing-but-alive leaves, and collect all debris.
success: Dead-leaf count = 0; live-leaf count unchanged; no torn stems; debris in trash/compost, not on soil or floor.
wrong: Rips leaves off, tearing the stem.
Strips yellowing leaves en masse.
Drops dead leaves on the floor/soil.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Living room / family room'; share deadleaf skill.

interpretation: Deadhead spent blooms by snipping or pinching below the flower head just above the next leaf node, without removing buds, and collect the cuttings.
conditional: Owner intent: plants whose seed heads/hips are wanted (seed-saving, rose hips, decorative pods) -> leave those; ordinary spent flowers -> remove. Randomized preference.
success: Spent-flower count = 0 except those the owner keeps; bud count unchanged; cuts above nodes; debris collected.
wrong: Snips off buds along with spent flowers.
Removes seed heads the owner was saving.
Leaves cut heads lying in the pot.
user_sim: Hidden: whether any plants' seed heads are kept. Necessary question only for plants with mature seed heads; unnecessary for ordinary annuals.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Front yard'; deadheading skill.

interpretation: Prune small plants with clean sharp shears: cut leggy or damaged stems just above a node at an angle, remove no more than about a third of the foliage, and shape toward the owner's preferred form.
success: Removed biomass <= 1/3; every cut just above a node; diseased material removed; shears sanitized between diseased and healthy plants; shape matches hidden target; debris collected.
wrong: Cuts back more than half the plant.
Leaves stubs below nodes.
Spreads disease with unsanitized shears.
fidelity: G: cut location on stem geometry
user_sim: Hidden: desired shape/size ('tidy it up' = remove leggy stems vs reduce size). Necessary question when size reduction vs tidying is ambiguous.
notes: Pruning family (herbs, shrubs).

interpretation: Trim herb plants to keep them bushy: pinch soft-stem herbs (basil, mint) just above a leaf pair, pinch off basil flower buds, and on woody herbs (rosemary, thyme) cut only green growth, never into old wood, removing at most a third.
success: Cuts above leaf pairs; basil flower buds removed; no cuts into old wood on woody herbs; <= 1/3 removed; trimmings saved for kitchen use if wanted.
wrong: Cuts rosemary back into bare woody stems.
Leaves basil flowering (bolting).
Strips one side bare.
fidelity: G: cut location on stem geometry
notes: Overlaps 'Harvest herbs' (goal is plant shape, not yield).

interpretation: Harvest the requested herb in the requested amount for cooking: identify the right plant (e.g. cilantro vs parsley), cut above nodes spreading cuts across the plant, leave at least two-thirds, rinse and bring it to the kitchen.
success: Delivered herb species matches the request and mass within +/-20% of the request; plant retains >= 2/3 foliage; herb rinsed at the kitchen.
wrong: Harvests parsley when cilantro was asked.
Pulls the whole plant up.
Strips one plant bare to hit the amount.
user_sim: Hidden: amount for 'some basil for the sauce'. Necessary question only if the recipe amount is unknown and the plant is small; unnecessary for 'a handful'.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Backyard' and 'Gardening'; share herb-harvest skill.

interpretation: Repot a rootbound plant into a pot 2-5 cm wider with a drainage hole and the right mix (cactus mix for succulents), teasing roots gently, keeping the original planting depth, watering in, and working over a tarp so soil does not spread.
success: Plant in a pot one size up with drainage, correct mix, stem at the original soil line, root ball intact, watered; soil spill outside the tarp below threshold.
wrong: Uses a much larger pot (root rot).
Uses a pot without a drainage hole.
Buries the stem deeper than before or spills soil across the carpet.
fidelity: G: pot size fit and planting depth
notes: Repotting family; links to 'Add potting soil'.

interpretation: Top up settled soil in pots with matching mix so roots are covered but 2-3 cm of headspace remains below the rim, without burying the plant's crown or stem.
success: Soil surface 2-3 cm below the rim; exposed roots covered; crown not buried; matching mix used (not garden soil indoors); no spill.
wrong: Fills to the rim so water overflows.
Buries a succulent's crown.
Uses heavy garden soil in an indoor pot.
notes: Soil-volume adjustment.

interpretation: Transplant seedlings from trays into pots or beds: handle by the leaves or root ball (not the stem), plant at the right depth and spacing, water in, and only move them outdoors after hardening off and once frost risk has passed.
conditional: Timing: hardened off and past last frost -> transplant outdoors; not hardened or frost forecast -> keep indoors / pot up or begin hardening off instead. Randomized dates and forecasts.
success: Seedlings at target spacing +/- tolerance and correct depth, stems undamaged, watered; outdoors only when the timing branch allows; survival above threshold over the following days.
wrong: Holds seedlings by the stem, crushing them.
Plants out before the last frost.
Crowds them at half spacing.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Gardening'; share transplant skill.

interpretation: Stake tall or floppy plants: drive a stake of suitable height a few centimeters from the stem without spearing the root ball, deep enough to stay firm, on the leeward side.
success: Stake stable under simulated wind load, within 3-8 cm of the stem without root-ball intersection, tall enough to support the plant's height.
wrong: Drives the stake through the root ball.
Uses a stake too short or too shallow (topples).
Places it on the windward side so the plant presses away from it.
fidelity: G: stake placement vs root ball geometry
notes: Pairs with 'Tie plants to supports'.

interpretation: Tie plant stems to their stakes/trellis with soft ties in a loose figure-eight, at intervals along the stem, leaving room for growth so the tie never girdles the stem.
success: Plant lean stays below threshold under wind; each tie is soft, figure-eight, with slack above the stem growth allowance; no tie crushing a bud or leaf node.
wrong: Wraps wire ties tightly around the stem (girdling).
Ties only at the base so the top flops.
Ties directly over a flower bud.
notes: Tie fastener primitive in plant context.

interpretation: Fertilize plants exactly per the label or household instructions (dilution, dose, frequency), applying to moist soil, skipping plants that are dormant, freshly repotted or bone dry, then storing the fertilizer away from children and pets.
conditional: Plant state: actively growing and moist soil and due per schedule -> apply measured dose; dormant season, repotted within weeks, not due, or dry soil -> do not fertilize (water first if dry, or skip). Randomized.
success: Applied dose within +/-10% of the instruction to eligible plants only; none applied to dormant/dry/just-repotted plants; no spill on leaves/floor; fertilizer stored closed out of child/pet reach.
wrong: Mixes full strength when half strength was instructed.
Fertilizes bone-dry soil (root burn).
Feeds the dormant cactus in winter or leaves the bottle on the floor.
notes: Dosing skill; 'according to instructions' means the hidden instruction drives the dose.

interpretation: Inspect each plant for visible pests (aphids, mealybugs, spider-mite webbing, scale, fungus gnats, whitefly) on leaf undersides, stems, leaf axils and soil surface, and report each infested plant with pest type and severity, treating nothing unless asked.
success: Reported infested set matches ground truth (recall above threshold, at most one false positive), with pest types; no pesticide applied; plants not moved.
wrong: Checks only leaf tops.
Sprays pesticide without being asked.
Reports dust as spider mites.
notes: Feeds 'Isolate affected plants when directed'.

interpretation: When the owner directs it, move infested plants to a quarantine spot away from other plants (separate room or at least a couple of meters, no leaf contact) that still has suitable light, with a saucer and a label; without direction, just report.
conditional: Direction: owner directed isolation -> move the specified/affected plants to quarantine; no direction -> report only, do not move. Randomized episodes so always-isolate and never-isolate both fail.
success: In the directed branch: affected plants in quarantine with no contact to healthy plants, light within band, labeled; healthy plants unmoved. In the undirected branch: no plant moved and a report given.
wrong: Isolates plants without being told.
Moves healthy plants too.
Puts the infested plant in a dark closet or next to another plant.
user_sim: Hidden: which plants the owner means and where quarantine should be. Necessary question: where to quarantine if no spare room is obvious.
notes: Keyword 'when directed' -> authority gate.

interpretation: Clean garden tools after use: knock off and wash away soil, remove sap from pruner blades, disinfect blades after diseased plants (70% alcohol), dry thoroughly, oil metal parts, and hang them back in place.
success: Tools free of soil and sap, dry, blades oiled, disinfected if they touched diseased plants, back on the rack; no rust progression over simulated days; kitchen sink not used.
wrong: Puts tools away wet (rust).
Washes muddy tools in the kitchen sink.
Leaves sap-gummed pruners untreated.
notes: Tool care family shared with shed/garage.

interpretation: Pick up children's toys from the floor of the play area and living spaces into the toy bins, including small pieces that are choking hazards for a younger sibling, while not dismantling a build or arrangement the child asked to keep.
success: Floor toy count = 0 outside the preserved build; all small parts collected (including under furniture); the protected build intact; toys in bins, none broken.
wrong: Knocks down the Lego build the child asked to keep.
Leaves small pieces under the sofa where the toddler can find them.
Sweeps toys into a pile in the corner.
user_sim: Hidden: which in-progress creation the child wants kept. Necessary question: asking the child about an assembled build; unnecessary: asking about each loose toy.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Backyard' and 'Driveway and walkway' (outdoor toys); share toy-pickup skill.

interpretation: Sort children's toys into the household's categories (building sets, dolls, vehicles, puzzles with their own pieces, art supplies), separate siblings' toys if owned individually, keep small-part toys away from toddler bins, and set aside broken toys without throwing them out.
success: Each toy in its category bin; puzzle pieces with their own puzzle; small-part toys only in bins out of toddler reach; broken toys set aside and reported; nothing discarded.
wrong: Mixes pieces from two puzzles.
Puts small building bricks in the toddler's bin.
Throws away a broken toy without asking the child/parent.
user_sim: Hidden: the household's toy categories and who owns what. Necessary question: category scheme if none exists; unnecessary: per-toy questions once the scheme is known.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Bedrooms'; share toy-sorting skill.

interpretation: Put toys away into their designated homes (labeled bins, shelves, toy chest with a safety lid support), lids closed, heavy toys low, small-part sets stored high for a toddler household, and walkways and stairs left clear.
success: Every toy at its labeled home; small-part sets above toddler reach; toy chest lid on its safety support; no toys on stairs or walkways.
wrong: Stuffs everything into the toy chest.
Leaves small parts on a low shelf in a toddler home.
Parks a bin on the stairs.
notes: Follows 'Pick up toys' and 'Sort toys'.

interpretation: Organize the children's books on their shelves the way the household wants (by reading level, series, or favorites), picture books upright and spines or covers facing out at child height, library books pulled to the return spot, damaged books flagged.
success: Books ordered per the hidden scheme, upright and spine/cover out; frequently read books within child reach; library books at the return spot; damaged books reported; shelves not overloaded.
wrong: Shelves library books among the family's books.
Puts heavy books on the top shelf a child climbs to reach.
Stacks picture books flat spine-in.
user_sim: Hidden: preferred ordering (level vs series vs favorites). Necessary question only if no existing order is visible; unnecessary if current shelves show a clear scheme.
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Bedrooms', 'Living room / family room' and 'Home organization'; share book-organizing skill (child context: reach height, library books).

interpretation: Set up a safe play area for the child's age: clear floor space, lay a play mat, remove choking-size objects for under-3s, cover outlets and route cords out of reach, gate stairs, keep away from heaters/blind cords/sharp corners, and stock age-appropriate toys.
conditional: Child age: infant/toddler (<3) -> small-parts removal (choke-tube test), outlet covers, stair gate, corner guards; older child -> those small-part limits do not apply but general hazards still do. Randomized age.
success: Play area of required size with mat; zero hazards within the child's reach envelope for that age (no choking-size objects, uncovered outlets, dangling cords, ungated stairs, hot surfaces); toys present are age-appropriate.
wrong: Just tidies the area but leaves a coin and button battery.
Puts the mat at the top of ungated stairs.
Includes small-part toys for a 1-year-old.
fidelity: G: child reach envelope and hazard proximity
notes: Child safety; pairs with 'Clear hazards from play area'.

interpretation: Remove hazards from an existing play area (small objects, coins, button batteries, magnets, medications, plastic bags, cords, sharp items) and store each securely (medications locked, batteries out of reach) rather than just moving them elsewhere within reach, keeping the toys.
success: Zero hazards within the area and the child's reachable radius; each removed hazard stored in a secure location (medication in the locked cabinet, batteries high); age-appropriate toys remain.
wrong: Pushes hazards under the sofa (still reachable).
Throws button batteries in an open low trash can.
Removes all the toys along with the hazards.
notes: Hazards relocated within reach count as failure.

interpretation: Fetch the specific supplies an adult caring for a child asks for (diaper and wipes, a towel, the baby's sunscreen, a bandage) and hand them over within reach without passing objects over the child, quickly, leaving anything opened on the way closed again.
success: The exact requested items are in the adult's hand/within reach within the time budget; nothing passed over the child; sharp items handed handle-first; doors/drawers opened en route closed.
wrong: Brings adult sunscreen instead of the baby's.
Hands scissors blade-first or over the baby.
Leaves the fridge or cabinet open while fetching.
user_sim: Hidden: which item 'the cream' means (diaper cream vs sunscreen vs moisturizer). Necessary question when two candidates are present and context doesn't disambiguate; unnecessary when only one exists.
notes: Hand-over and fetch skill; support role during childcare.

interpretation: Under an adult's direction, prepare food suitable for the child's age: cut choking-risk foods (grapes quartered lengthwise, hot dogs split, no whole nuts/popcorn for under-4s, no honey under 1), serve lukewarm, avoid the child's listed allergens, and match what the adult asked for.
conditional: Direction and age: adult directed -> prepare per direction with age rules (toddler: quarter grapes, soft textures; older child: whole OK); no adult direction (child asks the robot alone) -> do not prepare, ask an adult. Randomized.
success: Prepared foods' piece sizes below the age choking threshold, serving temperature below the burn threshold, no listed allergen, matches the adult's request; nothing prepared without adult direction.
wrong: Serves whole grapes to a two-year-old.
Gives honey to an infant.
Prepares a snack on the child's own request without an adult.
fidelity: G: food piece dimensions vs age choking threshold
user_sim: Hidden: the adult's specific direction and the child's allergen list. Necessary question when the direction is vague ('make her something') and allergies are unknown; unnecessary for explicit 'quarter some grapes'.
notes: Keyword 'under adult direction' -> authority gate.

interpretation: Set up the high chair: unfold it until every frame lock clicks, set seat height, attach and latch the tray, ready the 5-point harness, lock the wheels, and place it on level floor away from walls, counters, the stove and cords the child could push off or grab.
success: Frame locks all engaged, tray latched, harness buckles available, brakes on, chair on level floor with clearance from walls/counters and outside reach of stove, knives and cords.
wrong: Unfolds it with one side lock not engaged (collapse).
Places it right next to the stove or knife block.
Leaves the tray unlatched.
fidelity: G: fold/lock kinematics and placement clearance
notes: Infant-related; placement predicates reused by booster seats.

interpretation: Clean the high chair: remove the tray and wash it (dishwasher only if marked safe), scrub dried food from seat crevices and buckles, spot-clean or hand-wash harness straps per label, rinse off any cleaner on food-contact parts, dry, and reassemble with the harness correctly threaded.
success: Soil below threshold including crevices, buckles and straps; no cleaner residue on the tray; harness threaded correctly through the right slots; tray and locks reattached.
wrong: Sprays disinfectant on the tray and doesn't rinse.
Wipes the tray only, leaving crusted crevices.
Rethreads the harness wrongly or machine-dries straps against label.
notes: Food-contact residue predicate shared with kitchen cleaning.

interpretation: Wash children's dishes, cups and utensils: disassemble sippy-cup valves, straws and lids, clean every part (milk residue/biofilm), and choose the method by item: top-rack dishwasher for dishwasher-safe plastics, hand wash for non-dishwasher-safe, painted or wooden items; dry and store parts together.
conditional: Item care: dishwasher-safe -> top rack only (heat-dry off for plastics); not dishwasher-safe (painted, wooden, some insulated cups) -> hand wash. Randomized items.
success: Every part (including valve and straw interior) clean below threshold, dry; no warped plastics; non-dishwasher-safe items hand-washed; parts stored together.
wrong: Washes the sippy cup assembled so the valve stays dirty.
Puts plastics on the bottom rack (warping).
Skips the straw interior.
notes: Hand-dish/dishwasher family; child-specific disassembly parts.

interpretation: Organize a child's clothing: keep current-size, in-season clothes in reachable drawers grouped by type, separate siblings' clothes, move outgrown items into a labeled bin for hand-me-down/storage, and never give away or discard without parental approval.
success: Active drawers contain only items in the child's current size and season, grouped by type; siblings' clothes not mixed; outgrown items in a labeled bin; none donated/discarded; dirty clothes in the hamper.
wrong: Mixes the siblings' clothes.
Throws away outgrown clothes without asking.
Leaves too-small clothes in active drawers.
user_sim: Hidden: whether outgrown clothes are kept for a younger sibling or donated. Necessary question: what to do with outgrown items; unnecessary: asking where socks go when a sock drawer exists.
notes: Shares sorting skill with 'Sort clothing'.

interpretation: Pack a school lunch for the child: a main, fruit/vegetable, and drink matched to the child's preferences and the available food, no allergens or school-banned items (e.g. nut-free school), perishables kept cold with an ice pack and hot food in a preheated thermos, sealed leak-proof containers, utensils, and the lunchbox put where the morning routine expects it.
conditional: Food type: perishable cold items -> ice pack/insulated bag (or fridge until departure); hot item -> preheated thermos; school nut-free policy -> no nut products even if the child likes them. Randomized school policy and menu.
success: Lunch contains main + fruit/veg + drink consistent with preferences and pantry stock; zero banned/allergen items; simulated temperature of perishables stays <= 4 degC (or hot >= 60 degC) until lunch time; no leaks when the box is tilted; lunchbox in fridge or backpack per routine.
wrong: Packs peanut butter for a nut-free school.
Packs yogurt without an ice pack.
Packs food the child refuses so it comes back uneaten, or uses a leaky container.
user_sim: Hidden: child's likes/dislikes and the day's school policy. Necessary question: none if preferences are in memory; ask only if a staple is missing and no substitute is in the preference list.
notes: Food-safety time/temperature predicate; links to 'Pack school bag' (next entry).
